title: Medical Interpreter Certification Requirements: July 2026
summary: Get the 2026 medical interpreter certification requirements: eligibility, 40-hour training, exam fees from $530, and salaries up to $56,977.
body_markdown:
###


Your language pair is the deciding factor. CCHI tests Spanish, Arabic, and Mandarin orally; NBCMI tests Spanish, Cantonese, Mandarin, Russian, Korean, and Vietnamese. If your language appears on one list but not the other, that body is your path. One timing note: CCHI retires the CoreCHI credential on January 1, 2027, so factor that into your planning.


###


NBCMI's full oral certification totals $530 in exam fees alone ($40 registration, $190 written, $300 oral); CCHI pricing is comparable. Add 40-hour training, study materials, and language proficiency testing, and a realistic 2026 budget across most states (including California, Texas, New Jersey, and NYC) lands between $1,500 and $2,000. Employer tuition reimbursement, workforce development grants, and CCHI fee waivers can reduce that number, but budget for the exam cost regardless.


###


Yes, provided the program is recognized by CCHI or NBCMI - accreditation travels, so a qualifying online course completed from New Jersey counts the same as one completed in California. Confirm with the provider directly that their certificate satisfies the training prerequisite before paying. One exception: Oregon requires 60 hours, not 40, so check your state's specific requirement.


###


A training certificate confirms you completed coursework, typically the 40-hour foundational program. National certification (CMI from NBCMI or CHI from CCHI) means an independent body tested your skills through standardized written and oral exams and you passed. Hospitals bound by language access obligations read that distinction immediately: the training certificate says you showed up; the national credential says you met a verified standard.


###


NBCMI charges $40 for registration, $190 for the written exam, and $300 for the oral exam, totaling $530 for full oral certification in a supported language. The written-only Hub-CMI credential runs $230. Budget an additional $1,000 or more for 40-hour training, study materials, and language proficiency testing to reach the realistic 2026 total of $1,500 to $2,000.
